description: First entry with a communication area whose CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is ZEROS, so NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :177 is true: :178 sets re-enter, :179 moves LOW-VALUES to the whole CORPT0AO group, :180 moves -1 into MONTHLYL and :181 sends the map. This is the ONLY case in the folder that pins the TRUE side of :177 - case01 carries no communication area at all and cases 03 through 20 all arrive already re-entered - so the group move at :179 is proved here or nowhere. All seventeen xxxO items are pinned, which is what proves the group move reached every one of them - the ten unprotected items are X'00' and the six header items and ERRMSGO are then overwritten by POPULATE-HEADER-INFO and by :560. No map is received on this path, so no xxxI item is declared and no AID is read. The task ends at :199-202 EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID), which re-drives CR00, and the cursor is MONTHLYL because :180 set its length item to -1. Only CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT changes in the area carried forward, 0 to 1 per the 88 CDEMO-PGM-REENTER VALUE 1; the other fifteen fields are written out unchanged rather than left to be inferred, and every width is the one app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy declares, summing to the 160 bytes the XCTL at :548-551 and the RETURN at :588-590 both pass (practice B8). Nothing is written and nothing is seeded: inputs, expectedWrites, expectedFinalState, normalisations and expectedDatasets are all empty, and each empty member is a positive assertion that this path touched nothing rather than an absence of interest - CORPT00C issues no file command at all, every EXEC CICS in it being WRITEQ TD, SEND, RECEIVE, RETURN or XCTL. The two expected messages are the always-present spans, not DISPLAY output: :168-169 moves SPACES into WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) and into ERRMSGO PIC X(78) before any branch is taken, and :560 moves the former into the latter, so the eighty-byte value truncates to seventy-eight. DISPLAY 'PROCESS ENTER KEY' at :210 sits inside PROCESS-ENTER-KEY and is NOT reached, which is why no DISPLAY_LINE channel appears here while the sixteen DFHENTER cases carry one. No thank-you literal is emitted, and none could be: this program's only CCDA-* references are CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY at :193, CCDA-TITLE01 at :613 and CCDA-TITLE02 at :614, so neither COTTL01Y's CCDA-THANK-YOU PIC X(40), which names CCDA, nor CSMSG01Y's CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU PIC X(50), which names CardDemo - two literals that genuinely differ from one another - belongs on any path of CORPT00C. The unit is reached as a CONTROLLER_POJO: ReportRequestController is constructed as a plain object and mainPara is called directly, with no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container and no HTTP in the path (gate G51); the whole conversation - the communication area, the AID and the screen values - travels in the payload, with no server-side session anywhere (gate G37, rule R6). Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by reading app/cbl/CORPT00C.cbl, its copybooks, app/bms/CORPT00.bms and app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD - never captured from a COBOL run, which is impossible in this environment (risk R-A, practice B12); those inputs are read-only and appear here only as provenance (practice B3). The clock is pinned at 2022-07-19T23:12:34 and the code page is named US-ASCII rather than defaulted, which is what makes CURDATEO '07/19/22' and CURTIMEO '23:12:34' reproducible (practices B7 and B8). Java has no transient data queue, so EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD QUEUE('JOBS') at :517 is reproduced through an explicit job-submission port; the eighty-byte content is identical and the dataset key JOBS names the TDQUEUE(JOBS) that app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:499-505 defines as RECORDSIZE(80) RECORDFORMAT(FIXED) BLOCKFORMAT(UNBLOCKED) DISPOSITION(MOD). Two scope facts are recorded rather than silently resolved (practice B4). First, review_rules returns exactly 'No user rules provided', so no user rule governs this fixture; that absence is not licence to lower the bar, and the enterprise practices named above govern in their place. Second, this file's brief assigned it the EIBCALEN = 0 transfer to COSGN00C, but that scenario is already pinned correctly and byte-exactly by case01 at :172-174 and :540-551, and case03 pins the second XCTL site at :187-189, so the two gate G40 cases in this folder are case01 and case03. Re-pointing case02 at the same branch would have duplicated case01 - which the harness itself treats as a defect, since two cases sharing a description pin the same thing - and would have left :177 with no case at all, so the branch above is preserved as found (practice B5).
